summary: Continuation of the manna aggadah: bread was asked appropriately but meat was not; quail arrived immediately and lasted a month. The physical properties of the manna (flaky, melting), the claim that the manna fed like angels' bread, and Israel's fear that the manna caused infertility round out the passage.

display.whats: Bread asked appropriately, meat not; quail types and miraculous supply
display.hint: Why did bread arrive properly but meat bring punishment? How was the quail provided?
display.title: Bread from Need, Meat from Desire

learning.ahaMoment: God always gives - but the posture of the asking determines the character of what is given.
learning.memoryAnchor: Manna graceful, quail deadly: the difference was the spirit of the request, not the food.
learning.learnerQuestion: Why was the manna given graciously while the quail came with punishment?
learning.coreTension: Between requests to God born of genuine need and demands driven by excess or ingratitude.
learning.coreMove: The Gemara distinguishes: bread is a legitimate necessity, so manna came without shame. Meat was craved from excess desire, so quail came with fatal consequences. The spirit of the request shapes the character of the divine response.

takeaway.text: A request to God for genuine need is answered with grace; a demand born of excess desire is answered with judgment.

learning.learningBlocker: Students may think the Gemara is punishing Israel for eating meat; the critique is about the spirit of the asking, not the food itself.

quizSeeds.question: Why did bread arrive in the morning but meat at night?
quizSeeds.answer: Bread was requested legitimately (a genuine need), so it arrived properly; meat was requested from excess desire and arrived at the wrong time with deadly consequences

display.whats: Manna: between dew layers, flaky, angels' bread, and Israel's fear of infertility
display.hint: What were the manna's physical properties, and why did Israel fear it would leave no offspring?
display.title: Manna Between the Dew Layers

learning.ahaMoment: The manner of the manna's descent was itself the miracle: protected in transit, perfectly responsive to the hand.
learning.memoryAnchor: Between dew layers or dissolving at the palm - both images say: manna arrived exactly right.
learning.learnerQuestion: What do the different descriptions of how the manna arrived reveal about its miraculous nature?
learning.coreTension: Between Rav Papa's view (manna sandwiched between two dew layers) and Reish Lakish's view (dak mechusfas - it dissolves instantly at the palm's edge).
learning.coreMove: Both views emphasize divine precision: the manna arrived perfectly protected and perfectly suited for use. Whether sandwiched in dew or instantly responsive to the hand, it was never exposed to contamination or waste.

takeaway.text: The Gemara's two accounts of manna's descent both express the same theological point: the miracle was precise and tailored - protected in transit, perfectly available on arrival.

learning.learningBlocker: Students may treat these accounts as contradictions rather than two aspects of the same miraculous care.

quizSeeds.question: Why did Israel fear that the manna caused infertility?
quizSeeds.answer: The manna left no waste product, so they feared it also prevented having children (seed requires physical processes)

glossary.en: Quail - the meat God provided for Israel in the wilderness; its description is written one way and read another.
'Bread of the mighty' - interpreted as either the food of ministering angels or food absorbed by all 248 limbs without waste.
Ritual slaughter of animals according to Torah law; the Gemara holds these rules were given at Marah before Sinai.

rashiTranslations.he: לחם ששאלו כהוגן. שאי אפשר להיות בלא לחם: ניתן להם כהוגן.
rashiTranslations.en: 'Bread that they asked for properly' - since it is impossible to be without bread. 'It was given to them properly'

rashiTranslations.he: בבוקר שיש שהות להכינו: בשר שאלו שלא כהוגן. מתוך כרס
rashiTranslations.en: - in the morning, when there is time to prepare it. 'Meat that they asked for improperly' - out of a full

rashiTranslations.he: מלאה שהרי מקנה רב היה להם: שלא כהוגן. ירד להם עם
rashiTranslations.en: belly, since they already had abundant livestock. 'Improperly' - it fell for them at

rashiTranslations.he: חשיכה שעה שאינה ראויה לתקן אותה עד שעת הסעודה: כעין
rashiTranslations.en: dusk, a time not fit to prepare it until the time of the meal. 'Like
daytime' - by torchlight. 'And he set for them
a mealtime' - in the morning and the evening. 'That there fell
for them something requiring slaughter' - and this teaches
that the quail was something requiring slaughter.

rashiTranslations.he: וזבחת כאשר צויתיך. ולא מצינו בתורה
rashiTranslations.en: 'And you shall slaughter as I commanded you' - yet we do not find in the Torah

rashiTranslations.he: ציווי הזביחה היאך מכאן אתה למד
rashiTranslations.en: an explicit command of how to slaughter; from here you learn

rashiTranslations.he: שנמסרו לו הלכות שחיטה על פה:
rashiTranslations.en: that the laws of slaughter were transmitted to him orally.
'Spread out' - the quail was laid out before them
on the ground, spread out, 'litreidesh' in the vernacular.
'Bread' is good for young men, 'oil' for the elderly,
and 'honey' for infants; it is written 'shemen' with the vowel of

rashiTranslations.he: לשד השמן ואין זה לשון שומן אלא
rashiTranslations.en: 'leshad hashamen' [rich cream], and this is not the word for fat, but rather

rashiTranslations.he: לשון שמן לפיכך טעמו נקוד למעלה
rashiTranslations.en: the word for oil; therefore its cantillation mark is placed above,

rashiTranslations.he: ומ"ם שלו נקוד פתח קטן ולפי שהוא
rashiTranslations.en: and its mem is vocalized with a small patach, and since it is

rashiTranslations.he: סוף פסוק נהפך השי"ן לינקד בקמץ
rashiTranslations.en: at the end of the verse, the shin changes to be vocalized with a
large kamatz. 'Like thorns' - thorns, in the Aramaic tongue.
'And we set it in the oven' - such was their custom,
to roast their skewers in the oven. 'And it swelled'

rashiTranslations.he: מרוב שומנו הוא נתפח ונעשה עב:
rashiTranslations.en: - from its abundance of fat it swelled and became thick.

rashiTranslations.he: אתליסר ריפי. זו על זו ריפי ככרות: ותחתונה אינה נאכלת. מרוב
rashiTranslations.en: 'Thirteen loaves high' - one atop another, loaves like cakes. 'And the bottom one is not eaten' - from the abundance

rashiTranslations.he: השומן הנבלע בה וכל שכן העליונות: משתכח ליה. היו נמצאות לו
rashiTranslations.en: of fat absorbed into it, and all the more so the upper ones. 'Would be found for him' - they would be found

rashiTranslations.he: בין חביותיו שהיו ממציאין לו מן השמים: רב חסדא. חמוה דרבא
rashiTranslations.en: among his wine jars, having been sent to him from Heaven. 'Rav Chisda' - he was Rava's

rashiTranslations.he: הוה ורבו הוה: ובדיל רבה. בזכות הרב היה אוכל התלמיד: כתיב
rashiTranslations.en: father-in-law and his teacher. 'On account of Rabba' - by the teacher's merit did the student eat. 'It is written

rashiTranslations.he: ותעל שכבת הטל. והנה על פני
rashiTranslations.en: 'and the layer of dew rose,' and behold, upon the face of
the wilderness - when the dew would rise from
the earth toward the sun in its usual way, it was

rashiTranslations.he: נראה על פני המדבר דק מחספס
rashiTranslations.en: visible upon the face of the wilderness, thin and flaky.

rashiTranslations.he: למדנו שהיה הטל מכסה את המן
rashiTranslations.en: We learn from this that the dew covered the manna

rashiTranslations.he: עד שעה שהטל עולה לקראת החמה
rashiTranslations.en: until the moment the dew rises toward the sun,

rashiTranslations.he: וכתיב ירד המן עליו אלמא טל
rashiTranslations.en: and it is written, 'the manna fell upon it' - implying that the dew
was beneath. 'A box' - 'eskaron'
in the vernacular. 'Melts on the palm of the hand'
- 'mechuspas' is an acronym. 'Absorbed into the limbs'
- it does not leave through the intestines. 'After
they had sinned' - since they complained about it, saying
regarding the wretched bread (Numbers 21). 'Not
before them nor to their sides' - since they do not know
to which side the clouds are moving. 'But
behind them' - for they know they will not go back
the way they came, and those in front need
to exit at the rear of the camp.
'This' - the daf ends mid-word here; the comment (identifying 'ish' as Joshua, who ascended with Moses) continues on 76a.
